rules: Don't propose RANK($earnings_per_share) - RANK(X) for any X: this exact template drove 4 of 6 correlation rejects this round (X = volume, dollar_volume, or a short price/volume ratio-delta), all rho 0.92-1.00 against existing archive members regardless of which X was tried.

Drop $return, raw price deltas, and EMA-crossover-of-close (MACD-style) as a standalone or dominant leg: 9 of 20 rejects this round failed the cheap screen (|t| 0.15-0.93) this way, including wrapped in COUNT, TS_DECAY_LINEAR, TS_ARGMAX, or crossed with TS_RANK(volume) -- smoothing or longer windows don't rescue it.

Don't subtract a raw TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, w) leg against a fundamental TS_DELTA via CS_ZSCORE: the volume-delta leg is independently dead and drags the pair below the cheap-screen bar (0.54) even when the fundamental side uses a compliant 63-day window.

Before submitting a ($close-$low)/(stat) or ($close-$high)/(stat) style ratio wrapped in TS_MEAN or crossed via CS_RANK, check whether the denominator/other-field fragment already exists in the archive: 3 of 20 rejects this round were archive_subtree hits from swapping just one OHLC field or denominator field while a >=5-node fragment rode along untouched.
Dedupe each round's proposal batch against itself before submitting: 2 of 20 rejects this round (10%) were exact within-run duplicates, a pure wasted evaluation slot.
$close and $adj_close are the same series for correlation purposes (rho 1.000 this round); don't resubmit a formula with one swapped for the other expecting a different score.
A raw $volume <-> $dollar_volume swap inside an otherwise-identical ratio/TS_MEAN shape still collapses (rho 0.963 this round); stop using that swap alone as a decorrelation technique.

The strongest accepts this round crossed a two-fundamental product ($operating_margin * $accrual_gap) against a $dollar_volume magnitude or delta term (fitness 2.3-3.9, niches slow/mixed/low and slow/fundamental/low); this fundamental-product-times-volume-magnitude family is validated and worth extending to other fundamental pairs.
